summary: Evaluation of 14 days of closed-loop telemetry reveals strong overall glycemic control with an 86.0% Time in Range. However, nocturnal dipping (time below range peaking at 18.5% locally around 01:00) and afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia (time above range peaking at 32.1% around 16:00) highlight underlying tuning mismatches. The profile utilizes a flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, a 10-hour DIA, and aggressive overnight basal rates, combined with zero declared manual carbohydrate entries which forces reliance on UAM and SMB automation.

strengths: High CGM data completeness (98.7%) with stable closed-loop connectivity and device logging.
Strong overall time in range (86.0%) maintained via active oref1 automation (SMB and UAM).
Conservative safety limits (max basal 12 U/h, max IOB 25 U) prevent runaway insulin delivery.
issues: Nocturnal and early morning hypoglycemia (time below range reaching 18.5% at 01:00 local time) driven by aggressive overnight basal rates and a flat ISF.
Afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia (time above range reaching 32.1% at 16:00 local time) due to unannounced meals and delayed absorption under GLP-1 therapy.
Complete absence of manual carbohydrate logging, forcing the closed-loop system to rely entirely on reactive UAM detection.

recommendations.title: Reduce Overnight Basal Rates
recommendations.description: Overnight and early morning glucose values show frequent dipping and time-below-range up to 18.5%. Reducing basal delivery during midnight-to-morning hours will mitigate nocturnal hypoglycemia.

recommendations.title: Verify Meal Logging and UAM Dependency
recommendations.description: Zero carbohydrate entries are present in the treatment logs, causing afternoon postprandial peaks as the system waits for UAM momentum. Introducing structured carb entries or test meals will improve postprandial control.

profile_recommendation.rationale: While telemetry shows nocturnal dipping, profile changes must be made one at a time with careful patient verification. Keeping current profile segments while initiating structured observation of overnight glucose and meal entry is the safest preliminary step.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight glucose trends for 3 to 5 days to confirm whether early morning dipping persists before adjusting basal rates.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep current profile settings while closely monitoring nocturnal glucose levels and evaluating the impact of meal logging.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Without manual carbohydrate entries, meal bolusing relies entirely on closed-loop UAM detection and automated SMBs. GLP-1 administration further prolongs absorption kinetics.

exceptions.suggestion: Introduce manual carbohydrate entry or extended absorption handling on injection days.
exceptions.rationale: GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying flattens and prolongs postprandial absorption, which benefits from proactive meal announcements.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Initiate recording of manual carbohydrate entries for a 3-to-5-day period to enable pre-bolusing and improve postprandial afternoon control.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record explicit meal carbohydrate entries to evaluate postprandial glucose peaks against announced insulin delivery.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Continue monitoring CGM data and verify data quality while maintaining current settings.
Step 2: Initiate logging of manual carbohydrate entries for a few test meals to assess postprandial response and UAM reliance.
Step 3: Review nocturnal glucose trends after 3 to 5 days of consistent meal logging before considering basal adjustments.
education: Unannounced meal (UAM) handling relies on detecting upward glucose momentum before delivering insulin, which inherently results in higher postprandial peaks compared to pre-bolusing for declared meals.
GLP-1 receptor agonists slow gastric emptying, shifting carbohydrate absorption over a much longer window and interacting with closed-loop insulin delivery.
